text:
Tye Kartye was never drafted, and Seattle let him go on waivers. The Rangers claimed him, and the New York Post says he is making every minute count; Yahoo Sports called the Kraken's loss the Rangers' gain. Forever Blueshirts reports he has become a Garden favorite. Twelve points in 17 games, after 22 in 64 last season, and his ice time has jumped to just over 16 minutes a night from under 12.

This one looks mostly real. His own chances have nearly doubled, to 0.85 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.46, and the Rangers get 57.5% of the 5v5 chances with him on, more than seven points better than without him. He is shooting 19%, so expect a few fewer goals, but nothing else is propped up by luck; his linemates are finishing about at their chances. He plays a straight-ahead game (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him dumping the puck in more often than most) and kills penalties, the profile of a player coaches trust. Our projection has him around 50 points. Seventeen games is still a small sample, but the ice time says the coaches believe it.
headline: Tye Kartye, waiver claim turned regular
